bib.title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context", Freda Shi, Xinyun Chen, Kanishka Misra, Nathan Scales, David Dohan, Ed Chi, Nathanael Schärli, Denny Zhou. ICML 2023 (Proceedings of the 40th ICML, PMLR 202); arXiv:2302.00093v3, 6 Jun 2023.

COVERAGE: 68,910 of 68,910 chars, 18 of 18 pages, including appendices A-C. References were read for origins only. Nothing was skipped. Figures were not viewed as images: I have captions and whatever text the extraction gave.

CLAIMS

Shared setup unless stated:
- Data: GSM-IC-4K, 4,000 examples uniformly sampled from the 58,052-example GSM-IC. It derives from 100 easy GSM8K problems, each with one irrelevant sentence added.
- Prompts: 1 exemplar.
- Decoding: greedy (τ=0). SC means 20 samples at τ=0.7 with majority vote.
- Metrics: micro is accuracy per example. Macro is the fraction of base problems solved under every distractor variant.

- claim: Very few base problems survive all distractor variants under baseline prompts.
  number: no more than 18%
  setup: Best baseline is LTM at macro 18.0 (code-davinci-002, greedy, no instruction, clean exemplar). See PROBLEMS: 18.0 is over all 100 base problems, and Norm is 19.1.
  quote: "among the original problems that can be solved by baseline prompts with greedy decoding, no more than 18% of them can be consistently solved for all types of irrelevant information"
  where: p2; Table 3 p6

- claim: Micro accuracy falls for every technique compared with the base set.
  number: base to GSM-IC-4K: COT 95.0 to 72.4, LTM 94.0 to 77.5, PROGRAM 83.0 to 54.4, 0-COT 44.0 to 29.0
  setup: code-davinci-002, clean exemplar, greedy. The base set is the 100-problem easy subset.
  quote: "95.0 94.0 83.0 44.0" (Table 2 row, columns COT LTM PROGRAM 0-COT); "COT 73.5 70.8 72.4 76.2 8.3 2.5 6.0 6.3"; "LTM 74.9 81.5 77.5 82.4 16.7 20.0 18.0 19.1"
  where: Table 2 p3; Table 3 p6

- claim: Without SC, macro accuracy stays under 30% in all conditions.
  number: fewer than 30% (best 28.0: LTM, distractor exemplar)
  setup: Both models, all greedy prompt variants.
  quote: "The drop on macro accuracy is especially large, showing that fewer than 30% of the base problems are consistently solved after adding distractors."
  where: p6

- claim: Self-consistency is the strongest mitigation tested, but most base problems are still not consistently solved.
  number: over 11 points micro; best macro 45%. Table 3 overall micro: COT+SC 88.1, LTM+SC 93.4, PROGRAM+SC 74.6, 0-COT+SC 64.3.
  setup: code-davinci-002, clean exemplar, 20 samples, τ=0.7.
  quote: "Taking the majority vote from 20 samples, 6 SC improves the overall micro accuracy by more than 11 percentage points."; "the best macro accuracy among all prompting techniques is only 45%, suggesting that for more than half of the base prob- lems, SC fails to prevent the model from being distracted"
  where: p7

- claim: The correct answer is nearly always among the 20 samples, so distraction here is largely a problem of selecting the answer.
  number: 99.7% (COT, LTM); 96.5% (0-COT)
  setup: Recall within 20 samples at τ=0.7. This is an oracle measure, not what majority vote achieves.
  quote: "the correct answer for 99.7% of the problems is in the 20 sampled answers for both COT and LTM. Even for 0-COT, the recall of correct solutions within 20 samples is 96.5%."
  where: p7

- claim: A one-sentence instruction to ignore irrelevant information improves accuracy for the exemplar-based techniques, and it is that sentence that does the work.
  number: overall micro: COT 72.4 to 77.8, LTM 77.5 to 80.6, PROGRAM 54.4 to 56.7. Macro: COT 6.0 to 15.0, LTM 18.0 to 25.0.
  setup: code-davinci-002, clean exemplar, greedy. For 0-COT, micro moves 29.0 to 30.5 and macro stays 1.0.
  quote: "COT + INST. 79.0 76.0 77.8 81.8 20.0 7.0 15.0 15.8"; "Note that adding the instruction “Solve grade school math problems. ”alone does not significantly improve the performance, and it is the instruction “Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions. ”that makes the difference."
  where: Table 3 p6; p8

- claim: Using an exemplar that contains a distractor also helps, with no training or fine-tuning.
  number: overall micro: COT 76.8, LTM 80.7, PROGRAM 62.2. Macro: 14.0, 28.0, 9.0.
  setup: code-davinci-002, greedy, no instruction. Combining with the instruction gives LTM micro 82.8, macro 28.0.
  quote: "LTM 78.1 84.6 80.7 85.9 23.3 35.0 28.0 29.8"; "using ex- emplars with distractors (i.e., including problems with irrel- evant context) consistently outperforms using the original exemplars without distractors across prompting techniques."
  where: Table 3 p6

- claim: The type of distractor matters. In-topic is hardest, then role-name overlap, while number range matters least.
  number: COT micro: in-topic 63.1 vs off-topic 80.7; role overlap 68.3 vs none 76.6; in-range 70.2 vs out-of-range 74.6. COT macro: in-topic 10.2 vs off-topic 33.0.
  setup: Table 4 row for code-davinci-002, clean exemplar. Macro values here are computed on subsets, so they are higher than in Table 3 (authors' note). LTM is an exception on the role and number factors.
  quote: "COT 63.1 80.7 68.3 76.6 70.2 74.6 10.2 33.0 10.3 22.2 11.0 19.0"; "varying the numbers in the irrelevant information does not notably change the model performance, while the degree of lexical overlap with the original problem description matters."
  where: Table 4 p8; p2

- claim: More exemplars improve clean accuracy but can reduce robustness on harder problems.
  number: 1 vs 4 exemplars: GSM8K dev 60.3 vs 66.3; GSM-IC-4K >2 steps 70.8 vs 69.4 (with instruction, 76.0 vs 70.6).
  setup: COT, code-davinci-002. The 4-exemplar prompt comes from Zhou et al. 2022.
  quote: "COT 1 60.3 73.6 70.8"; "4 66.3 78.0 69.4"; "adding more exemplars can make the prompt less robust as it leads to some overfitting."
  where: Table 6 and p9

- claim: LTM holds up better than COT and PROGRAM as problems get longer.
  number: micro at 2 / 3 / 4 / ≥5 steps: LTM 74.9, 86.5, 77.3, 80.3; COT 73.5, 78.8, 66.4, 66.3; PROGRAM 59.1, 57.2, 46.3, 36.7. Row assignment is inferred, see PROBLEMS.
  setup: GSM-IC-4K, code-davinci-002 (the 2-step values match Table 3).
  quote: "the performance of LTM is fairly consistent across difficulty."
  where: Figure 4 and p7

- claim: The model upgrade does not fix distraction. text-davinci-003 is better normalised on micro but mostly worse on macro.
  number: LTM micro 76.3, macro 5.0 (code-davinci-002 LTM: micro 77.5, macro 18.0). text-davinci-003 base accuracy: COT 80.0, LTM 81.0.
  setup: text-davinci-003, clean exemplar, greedy.
  quote: "LTM 78.0 73.6 76.3 94.2 5.0 0.0 5.0 6.2"; "text-davinci-003 achieves better normalized micro accuracy than code-davinci-002, though its macro accuracy is mostly worse."
  where: Table 3 and p6

- claim: The instruction also helps on naturally noisy passages.
  number: code-davinci-002: COT 67.4 to 68.9, LTM 73.4 to 74.4. text-davinci-003: COT 68.2 to 69.9, LTM 70.2 to 72.8.
  setup: DROP football split, baseline prompts from Zhou et al. 2022. These are small gains, and there is no distractor-free condition.
  quote: "LTM + I NST. 74.4 72.8"; "LTM 73.4 70.2"; "the task is to answer a question according to a long passage that naturally con- tains irrelevant context."
  where: Table 7 and p9

- claim: Mitigations do not meaningfully harm clean-problem accuracy, by the authors' account (but see PROBLEMS).
  number: GSM8K dev, COT with vs without distractor exemplar: 59.3 vs 60.3; SVAMP 79.1 vs 77.6.
  setup: Table 5, code-davinci-002 presumed from the "mainly use" statement; the table does not name the model.
  quote: "COT ✓ 59.3 79.1"; "✗ 60.3 77.6"; "we do not observe a drop in ac- curacy when using exemplars with irrelevant information, adding natural language instructions, or both"
  where: Table 5 and p8

- claim: Two failure mechanisms are visible: using the irrelevant number directly, and derailing without using it.
  number: none
  setup: Worked outputs in Figure 3 and Tables 11-12. Example: the correct Lucy balance of $76 becomes $66 after adding "Lucy’s mother’s monthly rent is $10", for COT, LTM and PROGRAM alike.
  quote: "One common error type is wrongly using the number in the irrelevant sentence"; "the presence of the irrelevant sentence in the reasoning steps alone can still cause a wrong prediction"
  where: p6; Table 12 p16

- claim: The authors' conclusion is that mitigations help but the weakness remains.
  number: none
  setup: Whole study.
  quote: "a single piece of irrelevant in- formation can distract the models and substantially degrade their performance, even on problems whose clean versions they correctly solve."
  where: p9

LIMITS

Conceded by the authors:
- "We leave further investigation on the distractibility for other tasks and different language models for future work."
- The base set is an "easy" subset of GSM8K, selected as solvable by at least one technique. 60 of the 100 are two-step.
- 4K was sampled for cost reasons, and SC remains insufficient on macro.

Not shown by the source (my reading of its setup):
- It tests one added sentence. There is no scaling of distractor count or volume, no window occupancy, and no dose-response. It cannot support a claim that more marginal content degrades more, nor the note's 40-documents-vs-3 example.
- It involves no retrieval, reranking, compression, agents, tools, multi-turn sessions or long context. The note's listed fixes (rerank, dynamic k, compression) are untested here. Its mitigations are all prompt or decoding level.
- It has no attention or mechanistic analysis, so it does not show content "crowding out" signal or attention "drifting". It shows outcomes only.
- In GSM-IC the distractor sits immediately before the question (Table 1) and comes from a template. It is not naturally occurring, except in DROP, which has no clean baseline and so measures instruction gain, not degradation.
- It covers arithmetic reasoning only, and DROP's football split only.
- No confidence intervals or significance tests are reported. Some gaps are small, such as 70.8 vs 69.4.
- Macro depends on how many variants each base problem has, and is harsh by construction. The 4K sample is about 40 per base (my arithmetic). Table 4's note confirms macro rises when the variant set shrinks, so macro should not be quoted without saying so.
- SC costs 20 samples per problem, and the paper does not analyse cost.
- SC's 99.7% is recall, not an achieved accuracy. No method for selecting the right sample is offered; the authors only suggest one could be developed.

Dated:
- Both models are 2022-era GPT-3 family, code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. No newer model is tested, so the absolute numbers describe those models only.

BUILDS ON
- Dataset: GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021).
- Techniques: COT (Wei et al., 2022), 0-COT (Kojima et al., 2022), LTM (Zhou et al., 2022), PROGRAM (Chowdhery et al., 2022; Gao et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2022), SC (Wang et al., 2022c; Shi et al., 2022a).
- Instruction line: Suzgun et al., 2022; Sanh et al., 2021; Ouyang et al., 2022.
- Distraction precedents: Jia & Liang, 2017 (adversarial distracting sentences in QA); Li et al., 2022 (fine-tuning for robustness to noisy context); Liang et al., 2022; Patel et al., 2021 (SVAMP).
- Other data: Dua et al., 2019 (DROP).
- Psychology of irrelevant information: Hoyer et al., 1979; Pasolunghi et al., 1999; Marzocchi et al., 2002.

CODE
- Instruction prompt, verbatim (p5; Table 14 p18): "Solve grade school math problems. Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions."
- Distractor exemplar, verbatim (Figure 2 p5; Table 13 p17): "Q: Elsa has 5 apples. Anna has 2 more apples than Elsa. Liz has 4 peaches. How many apples do they have together?"
- Off-topic template, verbatim (Table 9 p13): "[ROLE] bought [NUMBER] tomatoes from the grocery store."
- Dataset location, as printed in footnote 1 (p1): https://github.com/google-research-datasets/GSM-IC

FIGURES
- Figure 1, p3: "Illustration of the considered factors when creating the GSM-IC dataset." Shows the three distractor factors at a glance. Image content not inspected.
- Figure 2, p5: "Prompt formats for the investigated techniques on the right, which are constructed from building blocks on the left". Shows prompt assembly and where the instruction and distractor go.
- Figure 3, p7: "Example problem and corresponding outputs by different prompting techniques". The strongest candidate: one irrelevant sentence, three different failures, faster than prose.
- Figure 4, p7: "Micro accuracies on GSM-IC-4K with respect to the number of required reasoning steps." LTM flat vs PROGRAM falling.
- Figure 5, p13: "Base problem distribution of GSM-IC with respect to the number of reasoning steps". Shows the skew to easy problems (60, 15, 12, 9, 3, 1).
- Non-figure candidates: Table 1 p1 (minimal example), Table 3 p6 (main results).

PROBLEMS

Embedded instructions: none aimed at a reader. The "ignore irrelevant information" text is experimental material.

Formatting of quotes and extraction faults:
- In quotes, line breaks are collapsed to spaces and the extraction's hyphenation and spacing are kept, so "prob- lems" and "I NST." are as extracted. Footnote mark "6" stays in one quote.
- Fractions are flattened: "110 ≤ ab ≤ 10" is presumably 1/10 ≤ a/b ≤ 10, and "norm(aM; M) = aMnM" is presumably a_M/n_M. Boldface is lost, so best-in-column marks are not recoverable.
- Figure 4 values arrive as a flat list. I assigned them to series by order, and only the 2-step values cross-check against Table 3. Verify against the image before using the 3, 4 and ≥5 values.

Internal inconsistencies in the source, from my arithmetic. All are worth checking before citing, and I could not tell whether they sit in the original PDF or the text layer:
- The text says 0-COT's SC gain is 35.5 points ("35.5 percentage points", p7), but Table 3 gives 64.3 − 29.0 = 35.3.
- "No more than 18%" is worded as a share of problems solved by baseline, but 18.0 is the raw macro over all 100 base problems. The normalised LTM value is 19.1. Safest to cite the macro number with its setup.
- "LTM achieves about double macro accuracy of COT" (p6): Table 3 shows 18.0 vs 6.0 (triple) with clean exemplars and 28.0 vs 14.0 (double) with distractor exemplars.
- "We do not observe a drop" (p8): Table 5 shows small drops on GSM8K dev, such as COT 60.3 to 59.3 and PROGRAM 59.8 to 58.6.
- COT+SC row: macro 29.0 / 28.3 with overall 30.0, where the overall exceeds both parts. Micro 87.6 / 90.1 with overall 88.1 does not fit a 60/40 weighting (about 88.6). Overall values do match the Norm column, so the step-split cells look suspect.
- text-davinci-003 LTM macro: 5.0 / 0.0 with overall 5.0 does not fit a 60/40 weighting (would be 3.0).
- COT 2-step is 73.5 in Table 3 and 73.6 in Table 6.
- Table 5 shows identical COT ✓ and COT+INST ✓ values (59.3, 79.1). This may be coincidence or a duplicated row.
